draft.title: Protons, neutrons and electrons
card: Proton
a particle with a positive charge. It sits in the nucleus, the small centre of the atom.
Neutron
a particle with no charge. It also sits in the nucleus.
Electron
a particle with a negative charge. It moves around the nucleus and is far lighter than a proton or neutron.
In a neutral atom, the number of electrons equals the number of protons. The positive and negative charges cancel out.
draft.remember: The nucleus holds the positive protons and the neutral neutrons. The light, negative electrons move around it.

a.q: Which particles are found in the nucleus of an atom?
a.why: Protons and neutrons are the heavier particles in the nucleus. Electrons move around the nucleus, so options with electrons are wrong.
a.clue: Electrons are found outside the nucleus.

b.q: A neutral atom of sodium has 11 protons. How many electrons does it have, and why?
opts: 11, because electrons sit in the nucleus
12, so there is one more than the protons
0, because the atom has no overall charge
b.why: A neutral atom has equal numbers of positive protons and negative electrons, so 11 electrons cancel the charge of 11 protons. No overall charge does not mean no electrons, because the charges balance.
b.clue: Neutral means the positive and negative charges are balanced.

problems.detail: The clue 'Electrons are found outside the nucleus' rules out every option except 'Protons and neutrons', because each wrong option contains electrons. It gives the answer away rather than hinting.
